name: E-invoice schema migration sandbox
demand: A real policy deadline exists, but the paying buyer market is still unverified. HMRC reports 2,285,900 live VAT traders at 31 March 2025; that is the regulated population, not the number of software teams that could buy this product (https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/value-added-tax-vat-annual-statistics/annual-uk-vat-statistics-2023-to-2024-commentary). A third-party tracker reading the Peppol Directory counted 22,149 UK VAT-number entries on 22 October 2026, about 1% of that older denominator; it calls this an upper-bound proxy and notes that directory listing is optional (https://einvoices.uk/data/uk-peppol-adoption). An HMRC survey found 29% of surveyed SMEs used structured e-invoices, excluding PDFs, but fieldwork was February–March 2025, the weighted effective sample was 495, and the survey measured invoice users rather than software-team demand or willingness to pay (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/electronic-invoicing-sme-usage-and-attitudes/electronic-invoicing-quantitative-research-into-small-and-medium-sized-enterprises-usage-and-attitudes). Search volume, installs, and the number of UK finance-software teams are unverified.
prices: The price evidence argues against charging for the sandbox alone: peppol.sh offers an unlimited free sandbox and charges €0.20 per live invoice, falling to €0.10–€0.16 at higher top-ups (https://peppol.sh/pricing); Invoicetronic offers a free sandbox and lists €0.02–€0.10 per invoice transaction, including validation (https://www.invoicetronic.com/en/pricing/); the European Commission provides a free validator, REST/SOAP APIs, and a conformance test bed (https://www.itb.ec.europa.eu/invoice/upload). Ironfang lists 250 free monthly validations, then £2 per 1,000 in its first paid usage tier (https://ironfang.com/finance). A broader UK G-Cloud Transalis eInvoice/Peppol service is listed at £450 per licence per year and includes a sandbox (https://www.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud/services/328294112934625). These are advertised offers, not proof of sales; exact pricing for a UK-spec migration sandbox is unverified.

revenue_proof.claim: Adjacent-market commercial evidence, not revenue proof for this product: Quadient reported French e-invoicing bookings grew eleven-fold year over year in Q2 2026 and included a multi-million-euro white-label agreement with a software provider. The reported period ended 31 July 2026; bookings are commitments, not recognized or collected revenue, and the offer was a broader e-invoicing platform rather than a UK migration sandbox.

copy_speed: High for generic Peppol validation and developer tooling. A Peppol.sh launch listing is dated 18 October 2026; its own site confirms a free sandbox and paid live delivery (https://peerpush.com/p/peppolsh ; https://peppol.sh/pricing). eFaktúra’s changelog says its developer portal launched 31 May 2026, its free sandbox began 30 May, and it moved sandbox traffic onto the real OpenPeppol test network on 10 June (https://developers.efaktura.sk/en/docs/changelog). These are adjacent products, not confirmed UK-spec competitors. No final UK technical rules are published yet, so availability of a genuine UK-spec sandbox is unverified (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/hmrc-transformation-roadmap-progress-update-2026/annex-summary-of-hmrcs-planned-activities-listed-in-this-transformation-roadmap-progress-update).
platform_risk: Peppol is now the UK’s announced core interoperability network, but HMRC says full guidance, standards, technical specifications, and legislation are planned by the end of 2027 to 2028; the implementation roadmap is due at Budget 2026 on 28 October 2026, five days after this assessment date (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/summary-of-tax-update-2026-simplification-modernisation-and-fairness/tax-update-2026-simplification-modernisation-and-fairness-summary ; https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/hmrc-transformation-roadmap-progress-update-2026/annex-summary-of-hmrcs-planned-activities-listed-in-this-transformation-roadmap-progress-update ; https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/chancellor-letter-to-the-treasury-select-committee-tsc-budget-2026-date). Government could supply or endorse a conformance suite; consultation respondents explicitly recommended sandboxes and pilots, and the Commission already provides a free API-backed validator. HMRC’s consultation response also notes that some existing MTD providers already offer embedded e-invoicing, creating a route for incumbents to bundle testing (https://www.gov.uk/government/consultations/promoting-electronic-invoicing-across-uk-businesses-and-the-public-sector/outcome/promoting-electronic-invoicing-across-uk-businesses-and-the-public-sector-consultation-response ; https://www.itb.ec.europa.eu/invoice/upload).
defensible_asset: Potential asset: a versioned UK rules engine plus a high-quality synthetic test corpus, migration diffs, and CI integrations that finance-software teams keep in their release process. That asset does not exist yet; UK rule details remain pending, while public Peppol standards and free validators make basic validation easy to copy (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/hmrc-transformation-roadmap-progress-update-2026/annex-summary-of-hmrcs-planned-activities-listed-in-this-transformation-roadmap-progress-update ; https://www.itb.ec.europa.eu/invoice/upload). Early defensibility is therefore low; it could improve through accumulated, permissioned edge cases and integrations, with moderate switching costs once embedded in CI.
build_effort: Unverified estimate. A demo using synthetic invoices and existing Peppol validation can be narrow; a dependable UK product needs versioned rules, migration comparisons, fixtures, API/CLI and CI integrations, monitoring, and careful handling of customer documents. A production build should be sized after the 28 October roadmap and again when the detailed specifications arrive; HMRC’s stated publication window is by the end of 2027 to 2028 (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/hmrc-transformation-roadmap-progress-update-2026/annex-summary-of-hmrcs-planned-activities-listed-in-this-transformation-roadmap-progress-update).
channel: Product-led inbound under a product brand: publish a free synthetic-invoice validator, CLI/GitHub CI example, version-diff guides, and documentation; distribute through opt-in developer communities and partner listings. No founder face is required. Do not rely on unsolicited messages to individuals or sole traders: ICO classifies sole traders as individual subscribers and treats stored social DMs as electronic mail; corporate-subscriber email is treated differently under PECR, while UK GDPR still applies to identifiable business contacts (https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/business-to-business-marketing/).
owner_hours_per_week: Unverified estimate: potentially 4–5 hours per week after the product and ruleset update process are stable, using agent-run CI, docs, monitoring, and first-line support. Roadmap/spec changes and enterprise support could push time above the constraint.
desk_test: Within one working day, prepare a product-branded, no-face landing page and a synthetic invoice/API-result demo; clearly label the UK rules as pending and accept no real invoices. Publish it in opt-in software-developer channels and ask for a paid pilot commitment through an inbound form. Continue only if a finance-software team commits to pay; otherwise keep this as a watchlist item until the roadmap clarifies scope. Response time and conversion are unverified.
red_flags: This survives the policy kill-check but is not yet a validated business. The immediate buyer is a narrow, uncounted set of software teams, while most demonstrated usage and population figures concern invoice-issuing businesses. Competing products make sandboxes free, and the mandate itself starts in April 2029; detailed UK rules may not arrive until the end of 2027 to 2028 (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/hmrc-transformation-roadmap-progress-update-2026/annex-summary-of-hmrcs-planned-activities-listed-in-this-transformation-roadmap-progress-update ; https://peppol.sh/pricing). Direct revenue for a UK-specific sandbox and willingness of software teams to pay for one are unverified. Recheck the 28 October 2026 roadmap before investing in a UK rules engine.
